'''Phyllis Zweig Chinn''' (née Zweig; born September 26, 1941) is an American [[mathematician]] who holds a professorship in mathematics, [[women's studies]], and teaching preparation at [[California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt|Cal Poly Humboldt]] in [[California]]. Her publications concern [[graph theory]], [[mathematics education]], and the history of [[women in mathematics]].<ref name="cv">[http://users.humboldt.edu/phyllis/vita.html Curriculum vitae] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190103011110/http://users.humboldt.edu/phyllis/vita.html |date=2019-01-03 }}, retrieved 2015-01-17.</ref>

== Education and career ==
Chinn was born in [[Rochester, New York]] and graduated in 1962 from [[Brandeis University]].<ref name="cv"/> She earned her Ph.D. in 1969 from the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] with a dissertation on [[graph isomorphism]] supervised by [[Paul Kelly (mathematician)|Paul Kelly]].<ref name="cv"/><ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=17149}}</ref> 
She taught at [[Towson University|Towson State College]], a training school for teachers in [[Maryland]], from 1969 to 1975, and earned tenure there in 1974, before moving to Cal Poly Humboldt.<ref name="cv"/> At the time she joined the Cal Poly Humboldt faculty, she was the first female mathematics professor there; the only other female professor in the sciences was a [[biologist]].<ref name="hay"/>

In 1997 she became chair of the mathematics department at Cal Poly Humboldt.<ref>{{citation|title=Class Notes|url=https://archive.org/stream/brandeisreview1814bran#page/n147/mode/2up|page=58|magazine=Brandeis Review|volume=18|issue=1|year=1997}}</ref>

Chinn is also an avid [[juggling|juggler]],<ref name="hay"/> and founded a juggling club at Cal Poly Humboldt in the 1980s.<ref>{{citation|title=Humboldt State University|series=Campus History|first=Katy M.|last=Tahja|publisher=Arcadia Publishing|year=2010|isbn=9780738580159|page=119|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=dcBoLlZQTdAC&pg=PA119}}.</ref>

==Recognition==
Cal Poly Humboldt named Chinn as Outstanding Professor for 1988–1989.<ref>{{citation|title=Class Notes|url=https://archive.org/stream/brandeisreview0913bran#page/56/mode/2up|page=57|magazine=Brandeis Review|volume=9|issue=1|date=Winter 1989–1990}}</ref>
She was the 2010 winner of the [[Louise Hay Award]] for Contributions to Mathematics Education, given by the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]], for her work in improving mathematics education at the middle and high school levels and encouraging young women to become mathematicians.<ref name="hay">[http://www.awm-math.org/hayaward/2010.html Twentieth Annual Louise Hay Award] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303233429/http://www.awm-math.org/hayaward/2010.html |date=2016-03-03 }}, [[Association for Women in Mathematics]], retrieved 2015-01-17.</ref>
